precepts.text: The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land; Ruth spoke of herself by that same word.
precepts.point: Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

precepts.why:
Ruth asked why Boaz took knowledge of her, “seeing I am a stranger”. She acknowledged what she was to Israel, and the scriptures use that same word of her people. “The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.”

The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land. Ruth the Moabitess spoke of herself by that same word, a stranger, and knew her place before an Israelite.

precepts.text: The bondmen and bondmaids of Israel shall be of the heathen round about and of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you; they shall be your possession. When we get into the kingdom this order will be in place.
precepts.point: Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

precepts.why:
Ruth called herself a stranger in Israel, and the law shows what the place of the stranger is. “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids. Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.”

“And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” The bondmen and bondmaids of Israel are of the heathen round about and of the children of the strangers that sojourn among us; they are Israel's possession, but over our brethren we do not rule with rigour.

When we get into the kingdom this order will be in place. Ruth, a stranger, fell on her face before Boaz because she understood it.

points: Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a mighty man of wealth of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Ruth asked Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace; and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Boaz came from Bethlehem and greeted his reapers, The Lord be with you; and they answered him, The Lord bless thee. When he asked whose damsel this was, the servant set over the reapers answered, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi, and reported how she had asked to glean and had continued from the morning with only a little rest in the house.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Boaz told Ruth to glean in no other field but to abide fast by his maidens; he had charged the young men not to touch her, and when she was athirst she could drink of the vessels the young men had drawn.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Boaz answered that it had fully been shewed him all she had done for her mother in law since the death of her husband, how she left her father, her mother, and the land of her nativity, and came unto a people she knew not before.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. Ruth answered, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord, for thou hast comforted me, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: At mealtime Boaz told her to come and eat of the bread and dip her morsel in the vinegar; he reached her parched corn, and she did eat and was sufficed and left.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men to let her glean even among the sheaves without reproach, and to let fall handfuls of purpose for her. She gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Ruth brought what she had gleaned into the city, gave Naomi what she had reserved, and told her, The man's name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Naomi blessed him of the Lord, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead, and said, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen.

note.label: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz

points: Naomi told her it was good to go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field; so Ruth kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest, and dwelt with her mother in law.
